finding: A fresh pinned-corpus scan finds 114 valid signatures, 11 key files, 7 unsigned files and 1 bad signature. A separate GnuPG keyring agrees on every verdict. All 123 paths shared with the older 228-file table have the same verdict and signature time; their raw SHA differences are entirely LF-versus-CRLF line endings. The sole bad file is missing the OpenPGP header/body blank line; an exact one-line repair and the preserved 2013 JPEG extraction both verify with the identical signature packet.
limitations: The pinned Git corpus contains 133 source-visible .asc files; the older table used 228 working-tree files, including 105 paths missing from this commit. Signature validity is relative to the specified public key and does not itself prove historical authorship or cover all messages. This is not a Liber Primus decryption test.
next_steps: Preserve additional original signed files with their exact bytes and provenance, then rerun the same verification and compare normalized bodies and packet timestamps.
question: Do the signed files in the pinned public Cicada corpus verify against the canonical key, and does the older source table describe the same file snapshot?
reader_question: Which archived messages have a valid Cicada signature?

reproduction.environment: Python 3 standard library and GnuPG 2.5.21 for complete offline replay; --check does not require GnuPG.

review.reviewer: Source program plus independent isolated-keyring verification

scope.exclusions: Files outside this pinned revision, unarchived signed messages, authorship beyond the public key, and any LP2 decryption hypothesis.
scope.parameters: 135 committed .asc paths, 2 source-scratch exclusions, 133 cases; canonical key fingerprint 6D854CD7933322A601C3286D181F01E57A35090F; source controls C1-C4. Supplemental 2013 opening comparison: four files, one exact header-line repair, and identical signature packets.
scope.procedure: Run the pinned source verifier in an isolated corpus and GnuPG home; independently verify every path with another isolated keyring; compare the saved table and source archive by path, raw SHA, signature verdict and packet time. A supplemental byte-level comparison checks malformed, repaired, other corpus copy and preserved JPEG extraction; isolated GnuPG verifies the latter three and reports BADSIG for the malformed one.
scope.representation: Every .asc Git blob at pinned revision f08b20b, excluding the source verifier's own two work/ control files; exact raw bytes reconstructed from 89 content-addressed blobs at 133 paths. A 1,459-byte extraction from the separately preserved 2013 JPEG is a supplemental comparator, not a 134th source-scan case.

summary: Of 133 pinned files, 114 verify. The lone bad copy is a malformed version of the signed 2013 opening message; its repaired and JPEG-extracted copies verify. The older source table covers a different corpus snapshot.
title: Which archived Cicada signatures verify?

visuals.caption: The archived table and pinned Git corpus share 123 paths. Every shared path has the same signature result and packet time.

reader_finding: Of 133 archived files, 114 verify under the specified Cicada public key. The one bad file is missing a blank line in its signed-message header. Its repaired copy and the original JPEG extraction verify; the source scan counts remain unchanged.
reader_limit: This checks preserved bytes against a specified public key. The bad copy cannot be treated as a validly parsed signed message until its header is repaired. The check does not prove who owned the key or cover all historical files.
